ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

An empty-stomach administration plan

A patient prescribed sucralfate for an active duodenal ulcer asks how to take it relative to meals. The clinician recommends the labeled empty-stomach schedule and reviews other medicines. What is the main practical objective of this counseling?

  1. Ensure systemic concentrations exceed those of a PPI
  2. Activate the drug through pancreatic insulin release
  3. Avoid all fluid intake throughout treatment
  4. Support local mucosal contact while avoiding clinically important drug-binding interactions
  5. Maximize simultaneous binding of every oral medication
Answer and explanation

Support local mucosal contact while avoiding clinically important drug-binding interactions

Sucralfate is taken on an empty stomach; reviewing and separating interacting medicines helps preserve their absorption.

Option explanations

Support local mucosal contact while avoiding clinically important drug-binding interactions: Sucralfate is taken on an empty stomach; reviewing and separating interacting medicines helps preserve their absorption.

Maximize simultaneous binding of every oral medication: Binding other medications is an unwanted interaction.

Ensure systemic concentrations exceed those of a PPI: Systemic exposure is not the therapeutic goal.

Activate the drug through pancreatic insulin release: Insulin release is not the activation mechanism.

Avoid all fluid intake throughout treatment: Routine fluid restriction is not required.
